title: Visiting Order
audience: adult literary readers who like grounded, character-driven realism and restraint
reader_contract: strictly linear: one afternoon, arrival to leaving; no flashback, no framing device
an interpersonal problem that no proof can settle; the turn is Lena's choice, made on camera
sensory, plainspoken prose; feeling carried by the mechanics of the visit and physical detail, never named
resolves by refusal: nothing is forgiven, the mother is not restored, the old imbalance is not healed, and Danny never learns the truth
theme_question: Is a kind lie a betrayal, or the last way left to keep faith with someone?
desired_affect: the weight of a kindness that costs the one who carries it
the loneliness of being the one who shows up
constraints: events happen in the order the reader receives them; no gimmick structure
the theme is NEVER spoken by a character or the narrator; it lives in one withheld sentence and in 'Mam sends her love'
no confession, no catharsis, no reconciliation, no absolution from Danny, no reveal that the mother 'really' loves him
prose earns feeling through concrete action; no told emotion, no cliche, no adverbial dialogue tags
Lena's choice is complicated, not saintly: pity, exhaustion, old resentment, and love all in it
